clue.text: The changeableness of the season-ticket holder?

definitions.text: The changeableness of the season-ticket holder?

parts.words: The changeableness of the season-ticket holder
parts.note: a season-ticket holder travels daily to work, so the quality belonging to such a traveller is read as interchangeability

explanation.surface: A wry question about how fickle a regular rail passenger can be.
explanation.walkthrough: A season-ticket holder is a commuter; the word for being exchangeable is built on the same root, so the clue reads it as the commuter's quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means capacity to be exchanged or replaced, and punningly the state of being a daily rail traveller.

clue.text: Caution advised to St Paul's visitor seeking Wren's monument?

definitions.text: Caution advised to St Paul's visitor seeking Wren's monument?

parts.words: Caution advised to St Paul's visitor seeking Wren's monument
parts.note: Wren's epitaph in the London cathedral tells the reader to look around if seeking his monument, so the Latin 'look around' gives the word

explanation.surface: Advice for a cathedral tourist hunting for the architect's memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London; his tomb reads 'Si monumentum requiris, circumspice', 'if you seek his monument, look around'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wariness or prudence, literally looking around before acting.

clue.text: Recording instrument said 0 show this measure

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds the same

parts.note: a meter is a device that records readings, like a gas meter

explanation.surface: A gauge is reported to display this unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of length, or poetic rhythm, is a measure.

clue.text: Unseen not studied

explanation.surface: Something never examined goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Not noticed by anyone; and not examined or watched closely.

clue.text: A number ready for the fray with the wind up

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a number
armed means equipped with weapons and ready to fight

explanation.surface: Many people prepared for battle but frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With the wind up' is British slang for frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightened or anxious, as one is after a warning.

clue.text: Train that is possibly in a state of rest

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A stationary train idles in a siding.
explanation.definitionFit: The tendency of a body to stay still unless moved, or sluggish inactivity.

clue.text: Desire to behead one of those greeting Macbeth

indicators.note: beheading a word removes its first letter

parts.note: three witches greet Macbeth on the heath in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A craving to decapitate one of the weird sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless craving or urge for something.

clue.text: A way of entering an American university? Try a long drink

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut
RD abbreviates road, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion for getting into an Ivy League college: try a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: A yard of ale is a very tall glass of beer, drunk in one go as a pub feat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet-shaped glass about three feet tall, and the beer it holds.

clue.text: Where Peeping Tom might feel at home in London

definitions.text: Where Peeping Tom might feel at home in London

parts.words: Where Peeping Tom might feel at home in London
parts.note: Peeping Tom spied on Lady Godiva in the Midlands city, so a London road named after that city would suit him

explanation.surface: A voyeur looking for a comfortable spot in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In the legend, Peeping Tom of Coventry looked at Lady Godiva riding naked; Coventry Street is a road near Piccadilly Circus in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A street in London's West End bearing the name of Tom's home city.

clue.text: The fundamental reason a relation got involved

indicators.note: letters that get involved are tangled together, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone explains why a family member was drawn into an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A justification or underlying logic for a course of action is its basis.

clue.text: Chariot, a success with a lot to carry

parts.note: a chariot is an old wheeled vehicle, a car in the poetic sense
to make a go of something is to make it a success

explanation.surface: A charioteer's triumph comes with a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is a quantity of goods carried by a ship or vehicle.

clue.text: Odd ruses of employers

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A remark about the strange tricks bosses play.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who employ something, in the sense of making use of it, are people who use it.

clue.text: A little one's modest contribution

explanation.surface: A child's small gift to a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A small child or tiny creature; and the widow's tiny coin offering in the Gospel story.

clue.text: Grief gets a state benefit

explanation.surface: Someone sad comes to rely on welfare.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word for sorrow; and unemployment pay handed out by the government in Britain.

clue.text: Article one found in post "Drains, hygiene, etc."

indicators.note: found in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: a post or position of duty is a station
an is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about public health appears in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts AN and I after the S of STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Public health measures such as sewers and clean water.

clue.text: Got to be made safe

explanation.surface: Something obtained must then be protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtained or acquired; and fastened firmly so as to be protected.

clue.text: Deal successfully with weight that's put on top of wall

definitions.text: that's put on top of wall

parts.note: to cope is to deal with something successfully
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Managing a heavy block placed on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The coping stone, the capping block laid along the top of a wall.

clue.text: Unyielding to requests for an old diamond

explanation.surface: Someone firmly refuses all pleas for an antique gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly refusing to be persuaded; and a legendary hard stone, once used to mean a diamond.

clue.text: Old iron, say

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former or old
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: Someone names an antique flat-iron.
explanation.definitionFit: To put into words or communicate a thought is to voice it.

clue.text: Peevish about upper-class cricket club getting aid

parts.note: sour means bad-tempered or peevish
U is the label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A grumpy toff's cricket club receives help.
explanation.definitionFit: Help given in time of hardship is assistance.

clue.text: Suffering from cold foreign season within limits of Sicily

indicators.note: within means one piece sits inside the other
limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: hiver is French for winter, a season in a foreign tongue

explanation.surface: A traveller catches a chill during a winter spent on Sicily's edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of Sicily' gives S and Y, and 'within' puts HIVER between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling with chill describes a person feeling the effects of low temperature.

clue.text: Milton's fair nymph "Under the glassy, cool, translucent wave"

definitions.text: Milton's fair nymph "Under the glassy, cool, translucent wave"

parts.words: Milton's fair nymph "Under the glassy, cool, translucent wave"
parts.note: in Milton's masque Comus a song summons the river nymph, who sits beneath the waters of the Severn

explanation.surface: A line of poetry about a water spirit beneath the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The nymph of the River Severn in the masque Comus.

clue.text: To say. "Keep mum" is nonsense

parts.note: sh is the call for someone to keep quiet

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an instruction to stay silent as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for rubbish or claptrap.

clue.text: The sign of a sore non-unionist

explanation.surface: A wound mark on a strikebreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The crust that forms over a healing wound; and a worker who refuses to join a strike or union.

clue.text: Benefit obtained from, for instance, a group

parts.note: as means for example, as in 'cities as London'
a set is a group or collection

explanation.surface: Something gained from a collective, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage or valuable resource is a useful thing to have.

clue.text: Express condition

explanation.surface: A two-word note about stating one's health.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or put into words; and a situation or circumstance.

clue.text: Pay what's proper

explanation.surface: Paying what is right.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a bill or cost; and an old word for fitting or suitable.

clue.text: Lightweight requires lots of oxygen

parts.note: a light weight can be one ounce, written in short form as oz plus one, and the gas is a molecule with three oxygen atoms

explanation.surface: A frail person needs plenty of air.
explanation.walkthrough: The light weight is one ounce, abbreviated OZ followed by ONE; the gas is made of triple oxygen atoms, hence 'lots of oxygen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of the gas whose molecule has three atoms, and loosely bracing seaside air.

clue.text: Start to speak about one drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin talking about a single drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin or come into being is to arise or initiate.

clue.text: Consideration of hospitality

explanation.surface: Considering how to welcome guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking an idea into account, as in entertaining a thought; and receiving guests with food and amusement.
